_purpose: Canonical machine-readable statement of HMTc Method v2.0 — the SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for how the program's method is described across heavymetalcertified.com. When the method changes, edit THIS file. The drift lint (tools/method-drift-lint.mjs, build-blocking in prebuild) fails the build if any page's prose regresses to a retired framing or asserts pooling as the universal method without the government-limit-default anchor. This is the sibling of the Part-2 'silent threshold deviation' guard, for prose.
label: HMTc-10 / Method v2.0 — government-limit default, selective occurrence for priority toxics and unregulated cells (CLAUDE.md Part 19)

statement.default: The default limit for any (product, analyte) is the strictest maximum level set by a credible government regulator (EU, Codex, FDA, WHO/JECFA, FSANZ, Health Canada), converted to the row's native basis — a lookup, not a computation.
statement.formulation_split: Where the law splits a limit by formulation, the standard adopts the law's own split and cites it.
statement.selective_occurrence_tier1: The four priority toxics (Pb, Cd, iAs, MeHg) are set to min(occurrence percentile, strictest government ML). That is limit-setting, not a status ladder.
statement.selective_occurrence_no_ml: Cells no government regulates use the occurrence value (or a not-material / process-screen determination) as the sole basis.
statement.tier2: Other claim analytes (Ni, Sn, Al, Cr-VI) adopt the government limit directly; occurrence is not computed unless no ML exists.
statement.occurrence_calibration: Where an occurrence cell is computed, a cleaner subcategory sits near P97 and a more contaminated one near P45; targets ~90% clean / ~40% dirty row-pass (measured 94% / 42% on FDA 2026 lot data), rolling up to ~80% program-monitored average.
statement.pool: The pool is the certification-relevant market: regulatory-equivalence, not geography.
statement.instrument: Certify against the subcategory split, never the element-wise-max envelope.
statement.unchanged_downstream: The four-status lifecycle (Certified, Remediation, Suspension, Revocation), the 3-lot baseline lot testing, the regulatory hard-stop, basis conversion, ALARA + the 80th-percentile ratchet, and the four rationale tags are unchanged. Certification requires every analyte at or below 100% of its published limit; there is no transitional overage band. All claim analytes are equal at the gate. An exceedance on any claim analyte enters Remediation unmarked.
